  "text": "At closing time, Martin found a woman sitting beside the library’s empty aquarium.

“The fish went in February,” he said.

“I know. I took them.”

She held a shopping bag on her knees. Something inside knocked against a jar.

“Are they coming back?”

“No. They’ve got a bigger tank now.”

Martin put down his ring of keys.

The woman opened the bag and brought out a small clay castle. Its highest tower was missing.

“I thought you might want this.”

He looked at the aquarium. Since February, someone had been putting lost gloves inside it. There were seven, none matching.

“We’ve found another use for the space.”

“I can see.”

She turned the castle over. A little water ran onto her coat.

Martin fetched a tea towel from the staff kitchen. She dried the castle while he lifted the gloves out of the tank.

“You don’t have to,” she said.

“They shouldn’t be in there anyway.”

He arranged them along the radiator. The woman set the castle on the gravel, slightly to the left.

“Looks smaller,” she said.

“Without the fish.”

She folded the wet towel and handed it back.

At the door, she stopped beside the noticeboard.

“Do you still need someone on Thursdays?”

“For the book sale. Mostly carrying boxes.”

“I can do some carrying.”

He took the volunteer sheet from its pin and found a pencil.

She wrote her name against the afternoon slot.

“Two o’clock?”

“Half past is fine.”

After she left, Martin checked the aquarium lid. Then he moved the gloves closer together so they would all get some heat."
